clue.text: Surroundings in which Mr Doonican has mixed feelings

indicators.note: the surroundings are said to hold the singer within them, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: surroundings make up the ambience of a place
Val Doonican was an Irish singer and TV entertainer

explanation.surface: A setting in which a famous crooner feels torn.
explanation.walkthrough: Val Doonican was an Irish crooner with a long-running BBC variety show; 'in which' is the container signal, and 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambivalence is the state of holding contradictory emotions towards something at once.

clue.text: A negative woman is quite different

parts.note: not is the word that makes a statement negative
her is a pronoun standing for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman who is not like the rest is a different sort altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: Something quite different is a separate, other thing altogether.

clue.text: A good friend to Holly

parts.note: a pal's name that sits right before the surname of the bespectacled 1950s rock-and-roll star from Texas

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a friend of a girl called Holly, but it is the singer Buddy Holly: the word for a chum came in front of 'Holly' in his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum or pal is a close friend, and that word was also the rock star's first name.

clue.text: Articulate lines about an Indonesian isle

indicators.note: the lines are placed around the island, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: verse is lines of poetry
Bali is an island of Indonesia

explanation.surface: Writing well-spoken lines about a tropical island holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective (well-spoken) but is the verb; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate a thought is to put it clearly into spoken words.

clue.text: Card game played quietly in a circle

parts.note: loo is an old trick-taking card game
p (piano) is the musical direction for playing softly

explanation.surface: A hand of cards dealt out quietly to players seated round a table.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is a historic card game; P (piano) is the music marking for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed ring or round shape traced back on itself makes a curve like a circle.

clue.text: To gossip about civic honour is perfectly OK

indicators.note: the gossip goes round the honour, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to natter is to chat idly, to gossip
OM is the Order of Merit, an honour conferred by the state

explanation.surface: Chatting about a mayoral award is quite all right.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour; 'about' wraps the gossip round it. 'To' and 'is' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it does not matter means the thing is fine and of no concern.

clue.text: Supply pique to order

indicators.note: letters put to order are arranged afresh, so these are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone sulking about being made to hand out provisions on command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' rearranges PIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish or provide them with what they need.

clue.text: Administer discipline for burglary

definitions.meaning: to train a horse or recruit into obedience
a forced entry into a building to steal

explanation.definitionFit: Training an animal to obey is breaking it in, and a burglar's forced entry is a hyphenated noun of the same words.

clue.text: Georgia lawyer fit only to be a social butterfly

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer
a bout is a fit or spell of illness or activity

explanation.surface: A Southern attorney suited only to the party circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' is a noun here, a bout of something, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is someone always flitting from party to party seeking fun.

clue.text: Instruct class to get a requisition

parts.note: to order is to instruct or command
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A teacher tells a school year to fetch an official request.
explanation.walkthrough: FORM is the British word for a school class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A requisition is a formal written request for goods, filled in on a document.

clue.text: Treatment which puts years on you and me

indicators.note: putting years on something adds them after it, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: us is you and me together
age is a number of years

explanation.surface: A rough handling that adds years to the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is handled or treated.

clue.text: Prime time to make hay, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the words describe how the entry is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a hay day would be a day for making hay

explanation.surface: Farmers know you make hay while the sun shines.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hay day' is said exactly like the word for one's prime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's heyday is the period of their greatest success or vigour.

clue.text: Make way for pets

parts.note: the word pets is the word step read in the other direction

explanation.surface: Stand aside to let the animals through.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, makes the clue word: STEP written back gives PETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To step back is to withdraw and give room, to move aside for others.

clue.text: To fix things up, change partners

definitions.meaning: to mend or restore something broken
to pair up again with someone new

explanation.definitionFit: Mending something is one sense, and pairing again (re-pair) is the other.

clue.text: Fiddle with a strongbox, but be very careful

parts.note: to play is to fiddle or toy with
a safe is a strongbox

explanation.surface: Tampering with a safe calls for great caution.
explanation.definitionFit: To play safe is to avoid risks and act cautiously.

clue.text: To increase pressure makes a market speculator sad

parts.note: a bear sells shares expecting prices to fall
down means sad, low in spirits

explanation.surface: Intensified stress leaves a stock-market trader miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: A bear in the stock market bets on falling prices.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear down is to press hard or exert force on something.

clue.text: Manage to get a canon to chase to and fro

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
a round is a song in canon, voices entering in turn

explanation.surface: A choirmaster sends a cleric dashing about the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' is the musical sense, a round like Frere Jacques, not a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To run around is to hurry about busily from place to place.

clue.text: Simple cleric without time for tea

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Simple cleric without time for tea (8)': CURATE gives most of CURATIVE but no reading of 'without time for tea' supplies IV; likely an OCR garble and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Simple cleric without time for tea

clue.text: Omit to mention having made a veloute

indicators.note: something made is assembled anew, so these letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Forgetting to say that you cooked a classic French white sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the final E of velouté, a French sauce; 'made' rearranges A VELOUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out of an account is to omit or skip it.

clue.text: Caerphilly cheese stuffed with Chinese fruit

indicators.note: the two words are packed with the answer, which sits across their join

explanation.surface: A Welsh cheese filled with exotic fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Caerphilly is a crumbly Welsh cheese; the letters run from its end into 'cheese'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lychees are sweet white-fleshed fruits native to southern China.

clue.text: Putting suet in pudding binds together

indicators.note: a pudding mixes its ingredients, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Adding suet to a steamed pudding holds it together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' is the anagram signal on SUET IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to join or combine them as one.

clue.text: Dan isn't suited to be a locum

indicators.note: letters suited are adapted into a new form, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dan is not cut out to cover for the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suited' rearranges the seven letters of DAN ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a substitute doctor or cleric who fills in temporarily.

clue.text: Repertory company on tour is rejected

parts.note: a cast is the company of actors in a play
away means on the road, off on tour

explanation.surface: A touring theatre troupe gets turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cast away has been thrown aside or discarded.

clue.text: A week before Edward appeared with a beard

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: A week before his appearance, Edward had grown facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'beard' is botanical: the bristles on ears of barley are awns.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass head with bristly awns, such as barley, is said to be bearded.

clue.text: Minor details right about one Roman road

indicators.note: the abbreviation is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
via is the Latin word for road

explanation.surface: Getting the small points right about one old Roman highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RT round.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are unimportant facts or details.

clue.text: See nothing but a recorder

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: You see nothing except a flute player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder' suggests a flute, but it is the machine that records TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A video was the cassette machine that recorded television programmes.

clue.text: RAF officer returns to the States for work

indicators.note: the officer comes back, read backwards

parts.note: PO is a pilot officer in the RAF
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An airman goes back to America to take up a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns PO round.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition.

clue.text: Charming little piece of self-indulgence

indicators.note: the answer is only a portion of the longer word

explanation.surface: A small dose of pampering is rather sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes something delicate and small in a charming, pixie-like way.

clue.text: I am beaten and held in custody

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am
pounded means beaten

explanation.surface: Battered and then locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or animals impounded are seized and held by authorities.

clue.text: Admonished for wearing informal clothing

definitions.meaning: in casual rather than smart attire

explanation.definitionFit: Being told off is one sense; choosing casual attire rather than smart clothes is the other.
